tasks.short: Administer employee insurance, pension and savings plans with brokers, providers and payroll.

steps.what: Collect employee changes and benefit elections.
Check eligibility, supporting documents and effective dates against plan rules.
Submit enrolments, amendments and cancellations to providers.
Reconcile provider confirmations, contributions and payroll deductions.
Resolve coverage and deduction exceptions with employees, providers and payroll.
Send benefit confirmations and correction instructions.

tasks.design: Configure change intake in the {HCM}, then use a rules service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to validate eligibility and reconcile {PARTNER_PORTAL} confirmations with {PAYROLL} deductions. The {WORKFLOW} presents submission batches and correction instructions for approval, sends approved notices and retains receipts; unresolved coverage cases stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provider formats, effective dates and plan rules differ. Interfaces and ongoing rule maintenance often cost more than the initial automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, scheduled jobs and configurable benefit events cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation development time without changing eligibility rules.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive coverage, disputed eligibility and provider corrections need judgement. Health data needs restricted access, and some providers may offer only manual portals.
tasks.human_edge: Protect coverage during difficult life events and negotiate a workable correction when provider and payroll records disagree.

ambition.what: Benefit continuity checks before extended employee leave

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rekeying and reconciliation to coverage exceptions and preventive checks. The specialist can prioritise interventions; authority to change entitlements or plan terms does not expand automatically.

reach.task: Validate benefit deduction corrections before the pay run.
reach.learn: Deduction codes, payroll cutoffs and retroactive adjustment rules.

evidence.claim: Structured enrolment checks and contribution reconciliation suit rules, integrations and approval workflows; savings are estimates.
Significant solely automated entitlement decisions require assessment under GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: The first release covers one plan and one payroll population.
Approved plan rules can be expressed as effective-dated checks.
Supporting documents are checked for required evidence without sending medical details to a model.
Estimates include consultation under national rules where required; external waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Which provider interfaces, exports and submission receipts are available?
Who may approve enrolments, cancellations and payroll correction instructions?
How many exceptions concern retroactive dates or disputed coverage?
Which employee consultation and access approvals are required?
research_questions: Can provider receipts identify acceptance at employee and effective-date level?
Which existing configuration can replace custom eligibility code?
new_work: Review submission batches and correction instructions.
Resolve unmatched records and rejected provider changes.
Maintain effective-dated plan rules and connector mappings.
Monitor receipt failures and reconcile completed corrections.

tasks.short: Maintain compensation and benefits compliance with EU and national rules, including required reporting.

steps.what: Review regulatory notices, reporting calendars and collective agreement changes.

loop.input: Approved regulatory notices and agreement changes with jurisdiction and publication metadata.
loop.output: Candidate obligations with exact source passages, dates and affected topics.
loop.check: Validate source passages and dates mechanically; a specialist checks scope and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; missing sources or ambiguity go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notices express changes in prose and use inconsistent structures; extraction does not decide applicability.

steps.what: Determine applicable obligations, interpretations, owners and deadlines.
Extract employee, pay and benefit data for required checks.
Reconcile totals, test required fields and investigate discrepancies.
Prepare required reports and assemble supporting evidence.
Review exceptions and approve the report for submission.
File the approved report and retain the official receipt.

tasks.design: Maintain approved obligations, owners and deadlines in the {WORKFLOW}; a bounded extraction loop proposes changes from controlled documents in the {DOCS}. Scheduled {DATA_PLATFORM} checks reconcile {HCM} and {PAYROLL} data and generate reports with evidence, while the approved release is submitted through the {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicability requires legal interpretation, while evidence is spread across systems. Reporting formats and national rules change.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable validation code and report templates reduce preparation work. Bounded extraction can surface source-backed changes for review without deciding their legal effect.
tasks.still_hard: Legal interpretation, collective agreements and incomplete historical records remain difficult. GDPR, the EU AI Act and national reporting and consultation rules need separate applicability checks.
tasks.human_edge: Judge materiality, resolve competing interpretations and take responsibility for what the company declares.

ambition.what: Monthly compensation and benefits reporting readiness decisions

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time resolving control failures before deadlines and less time assembling reports. They can recommend remediation priorities; legal interpretation and filing approval retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Assess whether job evaluation and pay reporting categories are defensible.
reach.learn: Gender-neutral evaluation criteria, comparison groups and limits of pay-gap statistics.

evidence.claim: Obligation registers, scheduled controls and template reporting are established deterministic patterns; this design is unvalidated.
AI used for specified employment decisions may fall within Annex III; intended use needs assessment.
The digest identifies gender-neutral job evaluation as relevant to pay transparency.
The digest documents Dutch works council consent requirements for specified HR data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: The first release covers a defined reporting obligation in one jurisdiction.
A legal adviser approves interpretation before executable checks change.
Reports have stable templates; unresolved narrative explanations remain human-authored.
Estimates include applicable national consultation work, access and a parallel reporting rehearsal.
unknowns: Which entities, jurisdictions, agreements and reporting obligations are in scope?
Which data definitions and control totals are authoritative?
Who can approve interpretations and release filings?
Which consultation, retention and data-access requirements apply to this employer?
research_questions: Which obligations can be tested completely from existing records?
Which reporting specifications support schema validation before submission?
new_work: Review extracted changes and maintain the obligation register.
Version approved interpretations and executable controls.
Investigate failed checks and document accepted exceptions.
Maintain report templates and verify filing receipts.

tasks.short: Research benefits and workplace safety practices and recommend policy changes.

steps.what: Assemble benefit costs, uptake and workplace safety indicators.
Review guidance, survey reports and current benefit and workplace safety policies.

loop.input: A fixed source set selected for the research brief, with dates and jurisdictions.
loop.output: A comparison table of practices, limitations and exact supporting passages.
loop.check: Verify quotations and source references; the specialist checks relevance and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per source; unavailable evidence remains explicitly missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Practices and caveats are expressed in varied prose, rather than a shared reporting schema.

steps.what: Discuss needs and practical constraints with employees and workplace safety representatives.
Compare policy options, costs, coverage and implementation tradeoffs.
Write a recommendation with evidence, risks and a proposed pilot.

loop.input: The specialist's chosen option, validated calculations and cited evidence pack.
loop.output: A recommendation draft with assumptions, alternatives, risks and pilot measures.
loop.check: Check every figure against calculations and every factual claim against sources; specialist approves wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported sections return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful recommendation must connect varied evidence and stakeholder concerns in prose.

steps.what: Challenge the recommendation and decide whether to sponsor further consultation or a pilot.

tasks.design: A {DATA_PLATFORM} job builds privacy-protected baselines from the {HCM} and {ERP}, while a bounded loop extracts cited practices from a controlled {DOCS} source set. A deterministic comparison tool feeds the {BI}; a second bounded loop drafts the specialist's selected recommendation for managerial review and any required consultation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence arrives in incompatible reports, and cost models are rebuilt for each proposal. Choosing a suitable policy depends on context that software cannot supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings, scenario calculations and source-linked drafting reduce repeated preparation. No breakthrough in policy judgement is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Research may not transfer to this workforce. Safety interventions need qualified input, and small groups can make aggregate reporting identifying.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which tradeoffs employees can accept and distinguish a credible intervention from an attractive but weakly supported benefit.

ambition.what: Quarterly decisions on targeted benefit uptake pilots

tasks.altitude: The specialist can compare and revisit more policy options during the year. They gain a stronger basis for proposing pilots; budget, safety and policy approval remain with the designated decision makers.

reach.task: Design learning support for a workplace safety policy pilot.
reach.learn: Behavioural learning objectives, practical reinforcement and evaluation of training outcomes.

evidence.claim: Reusable baselines, scenario calculations and source-constrained drafting can support policy research; no job-specific case is supplied.
The digest's report failure case supports checking generated claims against original sources.

assumptions: The tool supports policy research and does not make clinical or individual fitness assessments.
The initial source set is selected by the specialist rather than autonomously gathered.
Only necessary aggregate indicators enter the research workspace.
Estimates include access review and consultation preparation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which cost, uptake and safety indicators are reliable and lawfully available?
Which workforce groups can be analysed without exposing individuals?
Who supplies qualified workplace safety advice?
What budget and authority exist for a policy pilot?
research_questions: Which comparison measures remain valid across different benefit designs?
Which pilot outcomes can distinguish improved access from simple changes in enrolment?
new_work: Curate research sources and check their dates and applicability.
Review extracted claims and recommendation drafts.
Maintain scenario assumptions and privacy protections.
Track pilot outcomes and revisit recommendations when evidence changes.

tasks.short: Advise employees and managers on employment rules, agreements, compensation, benefits and job classification.

steps.what: Read an employee or manager request and identify its topic.
Clarify relevant facts, jurisdiction, agreement and the employee's concern.
Find current policies, agreement clauses and relevant employee records.
Interpret the sources and resolve conflicts or seek specialist advice.
Draft an explanation of the advice and available next steps.

loop.input: The specialist's advice position, relevant case facts and current source passages.
loop.output: A plain-language response with source references, assumptions and next steps.
loop.check: Check source versions, figures and references; specialist verifies that the draft preserves their interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing sources or contradictions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific explanations require prose; fixed templates can cover only standard questions.

steps.what: Explain the advice and discuss consequences with the employee or manager.
Record the advice, source versions and follow-up commitments.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake and case records in the {HELPDESK}, with permission-filtered retrieval from the {DOCS} and {HCM}. A bounded loop drafts explanations from the specialist's advice position and cited sources; the specialist approves delivery, while the {WORKFLOW} records approved advice and schedules agreed follow-ups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers depend on jurisdiction, agreement versions and individual circumstances. Search and case records often lack consistent metadata.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and versioned retrieval can remove repeated searches. Bounded drafting turns an approved interpretation into a clearer explanation.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, disputed facts and sensitive conversations require a person. Retrieval cannot establish that a source legally governs a case.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the concern behind the question, explain difficult outcomes and recognise when legal or labour relations advice is needed.

ambition.what: Guided comparisons of benefit options before employee life changes

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time locating clauses and writing repeated explanations, leaving more time for complex advice. They can offer guided scenario sessions; authority over employment terms remains unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an agreement interpretation brief for a disputed compensation question.
reach.learn: Agreement hierarchy, consultation routes and how to document competing interpretations.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, controlled retrieval and reviewed drafting are feasible support patterns; no directly matching product case is supplied.
Advice tooling should be assessed separately if its outputs determine significant employment outcomes.
Employment decision support may require assessment against Annex III depending on intended use.

assumptions: The proposed service assists a specialist and does not decide pay, classification or benefit entitlement.
Intake uses selectable topics and routes unclassified requests to a person.
Policies and agreements have identifiable owners, versions and effective dates.
Case logging uses approved text and structured follow-up fields rather than automatic call recording.
Estimates include permission testing and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Is advice currently recorded in a case system, employee record or shared mailbox?
Which policies and agreements are approved and reliably versioned?
Which questions require legal review before an answer is delivered?
Who may access individual advice records, and for how long?
research_questions: Can retrieval reliably filter by jurisdiction, agreement coverage and effective date?
Which recurring questions are fully answerable with approved templates?
How should the service detect missing facts before drafting?
new_work: Maintain source versions, coverage metadata and permissions.
Review drafts and resolve missing or conflicting sources.
Record agreed next steps in structured fields.
Review recurring unanswered questions and improve approved guidance.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward coverage assurance, policy experiments and complex employee advice. Better evidence supports more frequent recommendations; entitlement changes, legal interpretations and external releases retain explicit human authority.
reach: Payroll correction validation with payroll clerks.
Pay evaluation controls with equal opportunity officers.
Agreement interpretation with labor relations specialists.
Safety pilot learning support with training and development specialists.
skills_to_grow: Effective-dated benefit rules and reconciliation controls.
Data permissions, source provenance and GDPR requirements.
Scenario modelling and evaluation of policy pilots.
Clear advice writing and sensitive employee conversations.
Recognising when employment decision support requires EU AI Act assessment.
role.ambitious_version: Run a benefits assurance and policy-testing service: identify coverage risks early, compare targeted pilots and help employees understand life-change options through reviewed advice.

job.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
